run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T09:04:27Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a chaos-mesh fault injection into the ad service. The alert payload (start 2026-11-17T09:04:27Z, current 2.111) opened the investigation; the substantive error-rate deviation starts at 09:10:17-09:11:27Z, when a chaos-mesh JVMChaos experiment (spawned every minute by Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-return in namespace chaos-mesh from 09:10:06Z to 09:19:06Z) applied a JVM-level fault to pod otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg container ad. The ad pod emitted its first gRPC handler exception 1.8 s after the first apply, ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server spans switched from non-error to STATUS_CODE_ERROR, the frontend's GET /api/data and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans failed, and frontend-proxy's ingress and 'router frontend egress' spans became error spans. A low-level frontend-proxy ingress error rate existed before 09:10 and the alert's stated start (09:04:27Z) is not matched by the metric evidence; that earlier component and the alert rule expression remain unresolved. Errors were still elevated in the last available data point (09:24:27Z), after the last visible chaos Recovered event (09:19:02Z).

claims.text: frontend-proxy span 'ingress' with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR ran at 0-5.55 per 5m from 08:47:27Z to 09:10:27Z, then rose to 53.33 at 09:11:27Z, peaked at 301.11 at 09:17:27Z and was still 93.34 at 09:24:27Z; span 'router frontend egress' with STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0 until 09:10:27Z, then 47.78 at 09:11:27Z, peaked at 295.56 and was 86.34 at 09:24:27Z.

In the same 5m series across all services, the error-status series that rose above their pre-09:10 baseline were only: frontend-proxy 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'; frontend 'GET', 'GET /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' (0 until 09:10:27Z, 46.67-46.67 at 09:11:27Z, peak 294.44 at 09:17:27Z, 93.34 at 09:24:27Z); and ad 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds'. The other series returned in that view stayed at 0 or at their pre-existing ~1-1.25 per 5m level (ad and fraud-detection flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, fraud-detection ResolveInt, recommendation EventStream, plus zero-valued accounting/payment/frontend POST and cart series).

For ad's server span 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds', STATUS_CODE_ERROR was absent/0 before 09:12:27Z, then 119.62 at 09:12:27Z, peaked at 295.56 at 09:17:27Z and was 128.56 at 09:24:27Z, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET calls fell from ~254-327 per 5m before 09:11:27Z to 137.78, 40, 27.60, 40, 32.14, 20.22 per 5m after 09:12:27Z - i.e. most GetAds calls carried error status after the fault began.

Chaos-mesh JVMChaos experiments otel-demo-ad-jvm-return-gbjlm (09:10:06Z), -9f6n6 (09:11:06Z), -j2fmx (09:12:06Z), -plmnp (09:13:06Z), -ljkwf (09:14:06Z), -dlm4f (09:15:06Z), -4x48z (09:16:06Z), -m8wnc (09:17:06Z), -gzz89 (09:18:06Z) and -2xnmj (09:19:06Z) in namespace chaos-mesh each reported 'Applied: Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad' and 'Recovered: Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad' about one minute later (TimeUp); the 09:19:06Z experiment -2xnmj reported Started but no Applied or Recovered event inside the window.

The object creating those experiments is Schedule 'otel-demo-ad-jvm-return' in namespace chaos-mesh, which emitted Spawned/'Create new object: otel-demo-ad-jvm-return-*' events every minute from 09:10:06Z through 09:19:06Z.

Pod otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg emitted its first 'Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed@...' log line at 2026-11-17T09:10:17.866Z, about 1.8 s after the first JVMChaos Applied event (09:10:16Z), and repeated such lines until its newest available log line at 2026-11-17T09:19:21.741Z.

The ad container did not crash or restart: pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg was Running with all conditions True (Ready since 08:34:15Z), container ad ready and started, restartCount 0, lastState empty, deletionTimestamp null; deployment ad has readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, resources requests cpu 10m/memory 225Mi and limits cpu 50m/memory 450Mi.

CPU-limit exhaustion on the ad container is not supported as the trigger: its usage was ~0.006 cores before 09:10Z and 0.012-0.016 cores afterwards, far below the 50m limit, and the cgroup throttled-period ratio was already 0.098-0.182 while the ad error series was 0. The throttled-period ratio rose to 0.34-0.48 only after 09:11:27Z, i.e. concurrently with the error burst rather than before it.

The flagd fault-injection settings declared in ConfigMap flagd-config (namespace otel-demo, key demo.flagd.json) - including adFailure ('Fail ad service'), adHighCpu and adManualGc - are all ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off'; this is the ConfigMap state at query time (09:28Z), not proof of the runtime flag state during 09:10-09:24Z.

All 21 otel-demo pods listed at 09:28Z were in phase Running with restartCount 0, and all 21 otel-demo deployments reported readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1; this is pod/deployment state at query time and does not by itself show application health during the window.

Other event groups in the window belong to namespace data-recorders (StatefulSet/Job/Pod/PVC SuccessfulCreate, Completed, Provisioning, Scheduled, Started) and a cluster-scoped PersistentVolume VolumeFailedDelete; none references otel-demo or the ad/frontend/frontend-proxy path.

Faults injected by the JVMChaos experiments scheduled by otel-demo-ad-jvm-return caused the ad service's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds handler to throw during request half-close, returning error status that the frontend surfaced as failed GET /api/data and frontend-proxy surfaced as ingress and 'router frontend egress' errors; the 1.8 s gap between the first Applied event and the first ad exception, the per-minute cadence of the experiments, and the exclusive targeting of pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg container ad support this, but the injected class/method and the exact gRPC status returned were not observable.

The flagd runtime flag 'adFailure' (description 'Fail ad service') may have been switched on through flagd during the window independently of, or together with, the chaos experiments; the ConfigMap lists its defaultVariant as 'off', but the runtime flag state served by flagd could not be read, so this candidate is not excluded.

Errors were still present after the last visible chaos recovery (ad GetAds STATUS_CODE_ERROR 88.67 per 5m in the window 09:19:27Z-09:24:27Z, after Recovered at 09:19:02Z) and the ad container's newest log line is 09:19:21.741Z; a possible explanation is that the experiment otel-demo-ad-jvm-return-2xnmj (Started 09:19:06Z, no Applied/Recovered event visible) or an unreverted JVM mutation kept the fault active, but this is unresolved.

Read the chaos-mesh specifications for Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-return and the spawned JVMChaos objects (action 'jvm-return', target class/method, duration, scheduler) and stop or remove that Schedule to end the fault injection on otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg.

Obtain the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its evaluation window from the Prometheus/Alertmanager that owns it, and check the current flagd runtime flag state, to confirm whether the low-level frontend-proxy ingress error rate observed before 09:10Z is what triggered the alert at 09:04:27Z.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in the registered Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert each returned nothing, so the rule expression, evaluation window and the reported value 2.1111111111111107 could not be verified, and the alert's stated start 2026-11-17T09:04:27Z cannot be matched to a specific metric deviation (frontend-proxy ingress error increase was 0 in the 5m ending 09:04:27Z).

Jaeger returned no traces for service ad in 09:11-09:28:20Z or 09:24-09:28:20Z, and traces_search_by_tags for frontend with error=true and operation grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds returned nothing, so span-level error text and gRPC status codes for the GetAds failures are unknown.
Container logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-zsgq9 returned 0 lines, so the frontend-side error message for GET /api/data could not be read.
Container logs for flagd-5667b74b84-vlt8x returned no lines for 08:55-09:28:20Z, so flag changes made through flagd at runtime cannot be confirmed or excluded.

JVMChaos objects cannot be read with the available Kubernetes resource kinds, so the injected class/method/arguments of the 'jvm-return' experiments (including whether otel-demo-ad-jvm-return-2xnmj was ever applied) remain unknown.
Metric samples end at 2026-11-17T09:24:27Z, so the ad/frontend-proxy error rate between 09:24:27Z and the observation time (~09:29Z) is unknown, not zero.

The cause of the low-level frontend-proxy 'ingress' error rate that was present from the start of the data (0-5.55 per 5m before 09:10:27Z) is unknown; no status-code breakdown is available in the trace metric.
next_steps: Inspect Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-return and its JVMChaos children in namespace chaos-mesh (kubectl get schedule,jvmchaos -n chaos-mesh -o yaml) to confirm the injected method, action and scheduler, and disable the schedule if it is not intended.
Query the Prometheus/Alertmanager that owns the RequestErrorRate rule for its expression and for the alert's history to determine why it began firing at 09:04:27Z.
Check flagd's runtime flag state (adFailure/adHighCpu/adManualGc) as served on port 8013 for the incident interval.
Confirm from frontend logs or an unsampled trace backend what status/error the ad service returned for otel-demo.AdService/GetAds during 09:10-09:24Z.
